title: Cloud Engineer
tagline: Design and run systems on AWS, Azure or Google Cloud.
about: Cloud engineers design, build and operate infrastructure on public clouds. You'll choose the right services, set up networking and identity, keep costs under control and make systems resilient across availability zones and regions.
Nearly every company runs on the cloud, so the skills are in steady demand and certifications are widely recognised.
day: Design cloud architectures for new services

phases.title: Linux & networking
phases.goal: The operating system and network every server runs on.

nodes.d: Users, permissions, processes, services and package management on a real server.
links: OverTheWire: Bandit (learn the shell by playing)

nodes.d: Automate repetitive work with Bash, and know when to switch to Python.
links: The Missing Semester of Your CS Education (MIT)

nodes.d: IP, DNS, TCP, HTTP, TLS, load balancers and firewalls: what you'll debug every week.
Everything in infrastructure is versioned: code, config and infrastructure definitions.
Python or Go for tooling, automation and glue code.

project.d: Rent a small VPS, harden SSH, set up a firewall, serve a site over HTTPS with NGINX and automatic certificate renewal, and document every step in a README.

phases.title: Core cloud services
phases.goal: Learn one provider deeply; the concepts transfer.

nodes.d: IAM is the security perimeter of the cloud.
Private networks, subnets, routing and gateways.
Virtual machines, containers and serverless, and when to choose each.
Object, block and file storage; managed SQL and NoSQL.
Reliability, security, performance, cost and operational excellence.

project.d: Deploy a web app with a load balancer, autoscaling compute in private subnets and a managed database, all secured with least-privilege IAM.

nodes.d: Reproducible infrastructure with reviews and plans.
Event-driven systems with functions, queues and managed services.
Plan on pull request, apply on merge.

phases.title: Operate securely
phases.goal: Run cloud estates that are safe, observable and affordable.

nodes.d: Encryption, key management, logging and posture management.
Backups, recovery objectives and tested failover.
Make cost visible and owned by teams.

project.d: Terraform-managed dev/staging/prod environments with CI-applied changes, central logging, budgets with alerts and a tested restore from backup.

interview: Design a highly available architecture for a given workload.
IAM and networking scenarios: why can't this instance reach the internet?
certs: AWS Solutions Architect – Associate / Azure Administrator (AZ-104) / Google Associate Cloud Engineer
